atomic_issue.h100.r1.description: H100 atomic_issue protocol (tools/microbench/atomic_issue/protocol.json; probe atomic.cu: one CTA, W = 1 / 4 warps, U in {8, 16, 32, 64} straight-line atomics, lanes in blocks of L same-address lanes, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs). cycles(op, L) = slope over U of the per-U median (t_e - t_s) at W = 4 / 4 (per-SM admission interval), knots L in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}: ATOM <- atom: 67.6/67.6/67.6/67.6/67.9/73.9; ATOMG <- atomg: 61.6/61.6/61.6/61.6/62.1/67.8; ATOMS <- atoms: 1.3/2.2/4.0/8.1/16.1/32.3; RED <- redg: 31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6; REDG <- redg: 31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6/31.6; REDS <- reds: 1.3/2.1/4.2/8.4/17.2/34.6. Runs agree within 0.1 % everywhere, but the U = 8 point is absorbed by the in-flight queue (the sweep is not linear from U = 8), so the OLS max relative residual is above 5 % in every cell -> experimental per protocol. Diagnostic slope(W=1)/slope(W=4) at L = 1: {'redg': 0.26, 'atomg': 0.15, 'atoms': 1.0, 'reds': 1.0, 'atom': 0.17} (global atomics are a per-SM bound; shared atomics at L = 1 look per-SMSP: open engine question, kind 15 scope). Replaces the hopper.derived.atomic_same_address table (8.51 at L <= 4 rising to 37.1 at L = 32 for every class; a predecessor fit re-expressed over same-address lanes, no probe in this repository).

atomic_issue.h100.r2.description: H100 atomic_issue protocol addendum r2 (tools/microbench/atomic_issue/protocol.json addenda[0]; probe atomic.cu IND = 1: instruction i of the U targets base + warp x 512 KiB + i x 4 KiB + b x 128 B, no two instructions of a rep share a line, lanes in blocks of L same-address lanes so L = 1 is 32 distinct lines per instruction; U in {16, 32, 64, 128}, W = 1 / 4, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs in one job; GPU GPU-2aaf46f6-a1da-fb47-c390-6732377364b0). cycles(op, L) = (med(U=128) - med(U=64)) / 64 / 4 at W = 4, knots L in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}: atomg 74.1/74.0/74.1/74.1/75.6/74.0 (experimental, steady 0.41, agree 0.0008, OLS resid 1.41); redg 32.0/32.0/32.0/32.0/32.0/32.0 (measured, steady 0.00, agree 0.0000, OLS resid 0.11); atom 79.0/79.0/79.1/79.1/80.0/79.0 (experimental, steady 0.54, agree 0.0002, OLS resid 0.87). Control (same-job r1-style same-address slope / 4, L = 1, W = 4): atomg 61.75/61.75 vs r1 61.63, redg 31.61/31.61 vs r1 31.61 -> ok. Installed (measured cells only): RED, REDG; the other classes keep r1. Finding: with 32 distinct lines per instruction the per-SM interval is not lower than the r1 same-address figure (the same-line follow-on hypothesis of full-gpu-chain-report.md 8.6 is refuted); the cost tracks the lines a warp-wide atomic touches, which the axis atomic_same_address_lanes does not see (the stream-K fixup ATOMG is 32 lanes x 4 B in ONE line) -> addendum r3 measures the lines axis. r1 values kept in the source description of atomic_issue.h100.r1.

atomic_issue.h100.r3.description: H100 atomic_issue protocol addendum r3 (tools/microbench/atomic_issue/protocol.json addenda[1]; probe atomic.cu IND = 1 with block stride S: instruction i at base + warp x 512 KiB + i x 4 KiB, block b of L same-address lanes at + b x S; U in {16, 32, 64, 128}, W = 1 / 4, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs in one job; GPU GPU-2aaf46f6-a1da-fb47-c390-6732377364b0). cycles = (med(U=128) - med(U=64)) / 64 / 4 at W = 4. Lines sweep (L = 1, S = 4..128 -> cache_line_count 1/2/4/8/16/32; m = measured, e = experimental per cell): atomg 5.8/11.5/23.1/46.2/55.4/74.1 (eeeeee); redg 5.0/10.0/20.0/40.0/48.0/32.0 (mmmmmm); atom 6.0/12.2/24.3/48.6/58.2/79.0 (eeeeee). Same-word sweep (S = 4, one line, L = 1/2/4/8/16/32 lanes per word): atomg 5.8/6.9/12.0/25.6/49.7/74.0 (spread 11.6); redg 5.0/6.0/8.0/16.0/32.0/32.0 (spread 5.4); atom 6.0/8.2/13.1/27.6/53.0/79.0 (spread 12.1) -> open item: a second dependence on same-word lanes (about 1 cycle per lane for redg, 2.3 for atomg) that the single-axis leaf does not carry; the installed knots are the L = 1 (all words distinct) values. Controls: r1 same-address cell ok, r2 S = 128 cells ok (redg 32.00 vs 32.0). Installed (all six knots measured): RED, REDG on axis cache_line_count (the instruction's distinct 128 B lines); ATOMG / ATOM not installed: the W = 4 sweep of returning atomics is not steady over U (increment 32->64 vs 64->128 differ by about 40 %: the per-warp return path saturates near 64 outstanding ATOMG), they keep their previous leaf (atomic_same_address_lanes axis). Finding: a coalesced warp-wide global atomic (32 lanes x 4 B in one line, the stream-K fixup / atomicAdd epilogue pattern) costs about 5-6 cycles per SM on both devices against 61.6 / 58 installed; the r1 / r2 figures were the 32-distinct-lines pattern.

atomic_issue.h100.r5.description: H100 atomic_issue protocol addendum r5 (tools/microbench/atomic_issue/protocol.json addenda[3]; probe atomic.cu IND = 1, W = 16 warps (four per SMSP), block stride S, instruction i at base + warp x 512 KiB + i x 4 KiB, U in {16, 32, 64}, --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs in one job; GPU GPU-f266a6de-37fb-c58b-e769-cd3e7b3a6e93). cycles = mean over U in {32, 64} of T(U) / U / 16 (saturated per-SM interval; gate flat <= 10 %, run agreement <= 5 %). Lines sweep (L = 1, S = 4..128 -> cache_line_count 1/2/4/8/16/32): atomg 4.6/9.3/18.7/37.1/44.3/56.7 (flat max 0.029, agree max 0.0020); atom 4.7/9.5/18.9/37.3/44.7/58.3 (flat max 0.037, agree max 0.0022); redg 4.6/9.4/18.9/38.0/45.7/30.6 (flat max 0.034, agree max 0.0006) (control vs the r3 REDG install: 1 lines 4.63 vs r3 5.0, 2 lines 9.44 vs r3 10.0, 4 lines 18.94 vs r3 20.0, 8 lines 38.01 vs r3 40.0, 16 lines 45.67 vs r3 48.0, 32 lines 30.58 vs r3 32.0). Same-word sweep (S = 4, one line, L lanes per word 1/2/4/8/16/32): atomg 4.6/5.7/9.4/20.2/40.8/58.2 (spread 11.6); atom 4.7/6.2/10.0/21.1/41.8/59.7 (spread 11.7); redg 4.6/5.7/7.7/15.3/30.6/30.7 (spread 5.6) -> open item carried from r3 (second dependence on same-word lanes, about 2.3 cycles per lane for atomg; the leaf is single-axis, knots are the all-words-distinct values). Installed: ATOMG <- atomg, ATOM <- atom on axis cache_line_count (replaces the r1 / r2 atomic_same_address_lanes tables: those were the 32-distinct-lines pattern, 61.6 / 67.6 (h100) and 58.1 / 55.3 (b300) at every L); RED / REDG keep r3. Gate history: the r2-r4 increment gates were not met by returning atomics (concave issue back-pressure window) although the value reproduced; the r5 gate was redefined with user authorisation before this run.

barrier_release.h100.r4.description: H100 barrier_release protocol v2 (tools/microbench/barrier_release/protocol-v2.json + addendum 2026-11-05; probes verbatim, --reps 256 --launches 8, two runs; sm_90a runs only the mbarrier cells of sync_mb / sync_xw -- the tcgen05 cells are unrealised there). mbarrier.release = E[t_w - t_s | try_wait waiter, delay >= 4000] - o_s - o_w - r_sync = 87.93 (run a 88.27 / b 87.60, se 0.54 each, agreement 0.8 %; r13 value 88.30 from h100-r1/r2) -> measured. cta.release(W) = E[bar.cta.wW.warplast] - o_s(12) - o_w(7) = 16.0 for W = 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 in both runs (se 0; W = 2 / 32 negative: phase wrap, reported) -> measured, same as crossings.cta_release.h100.r1. cluster.release(S) = E[bar.cluster.cS.relaxed.arriver] - o_s(28) - o_w(13) = 86 / 81 / 81 for S = 2 / 4 / 8 (deterministic in both runs) -> measured; the .release arrive form measures 739 / 731 / 731 (MEMBAR.ALL.GPU + ERRBAR before UCGABAR_ARV, ~650 cycles of fence, reported, not installed); replaces the hopper-prototype fit 164-202 (hopper.cluster.sync.release). cp_async.arrival = (median noinc - issue) - (median arrive - issue) = 15.5 (16 / 15, se 1.5, agreement 6.5 % > 5 %) -> experimental (r13 value 18.0 from h100-r1).

barrier_release.h100.r4.experimental.description: Same run: cp_async.arrival 15.5 (16 / 15), se 1.5 cycles, run agreement 6.5 % -- outside the 5 % rule, experimental per protocol (replaces the r13 18.0, itself experimental).

barrier_release.h100.r4.tw_only.description: H100 barrier_release protocol-v2 addendum 2026-11-06: SYNCS.PHASECHK result_latency_cycles = OLS slope of the tw_only chain medians over U (42.932, interior resid 1.5%, runs a/b identical) - modal control-word stall 5 of the unit's @!P BRA in sync_mb SASS = 37.93; completion_latency_cycles equal. Derivation tools/microbench/barrier_release/model_tw_only.py; experimental. Literal acceptance not met: U=1 point residual 6.2 / 7.3 % and the window's first unit carries BRA stall 6 (TRYWAIT 1 + BRA 6 = 7, same sum); interior units (U >= 2, units 2..N-1) are exactly 43.0 / unit; value = interior slope - 5

branch_basic.h100.v1.description: branch_basic protocol v2 (tools/microbench/branch_basic/protocol-v2.json; installation from the version 1 readings, frozen before any replay with a changed engine or tree). Y1 YIELD result/completion = C + 2, C = mean over v.yield1, .s1, .y0, .alu and v.yield2 / 2 of (sample total - v.nop), 2 = stall of the NOP the YIELD replaced: (48.84 + 47.54 + 48.23 + 48.14 + 47.42) / 5 + 2 = 50.03. R1 control.reconvergence.control_envelope = affine intercept 0, slope 0: a BSSY holds the warp for its stall field only. R2 BSYNC result/completion = 13.0: next issue no earlier than the BSYNC's issue + result latency, max with its stall, every dynamic BSYNC instance alike (row behind the BSYNC in w.if.nt / w.if.t, regions 2-4, per execution: 12.96 / 12.96; in a divergent region the non-final path's share is booked a few instructions early, 12.9 extra per extra path in all). B1 control.branch.control_envelope(branch_taken = 1) = 10.00: time from the BRA's issue to the issue of its target, loop back-edges per trip: s.loop 10.58, v.nop 9.88, w.ubr.nt 9.53, w.if.nt 9.63, w.ubr.t 10.40; branch_taken = 0 stays 0.

constant_launch.h100.r3.description: H100 constant_launch protocols v2 + v3 (tools/microbench/constant_launch/protocol-v2.json, protocol-v3.json, frozen before data; probes constlaunch_v2.cu / constlaunch_v3.cu: 16 dependent constant loads per traversal, two traversals, CS2R after every load, ncu --cache-control all, 34 launches, first 2 dropped, two runs; per-load latency = clock delta minus the installed result latency of the single in-between op (IMAD / USHF 4)). Vector path (LDC R, c[0x0][R]; v2 run h100-r2, reproduced by the v3 control within 0 %): bank-0 first 30.0 / second 30.0 / load 0 30.0, measured -> bank0_access_cycles = 30.0, engine rule (protocol-v3 path split): a vector LDC to bank 0 returns now + 30 (parameter / driver bank resident at launch). Uniform path (ULDC / LDCU with UR index, v3 run h100-r3): bank-0 first 288.5 (experimental), second 68.0 (measured); bank-3 first 270.0 (experimental), second 68.0 (measured) -> no uniform rule (declared condition: both measured and second within 10 % of first); uniform loads keep the miss / hit / same-line / in-flight rules. Cold miss: vector bank-3 first 817.2 (measured) vs uniform 270.0 (experimental) -> miss_latency_cycles unchanged (declared condition: both measured and within 10 %). Not installed (A/B arms only): the v2 'every bank-0 access' rule (task/lifecycle-v3 913d77d, arm $A/merge/cbi).

constant_paths.h100.v1.experimental.description: H100 constant_paths v1 experimental fields (tools/microbench/constant_paths/protocol.json; data $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/warp_issue/h100, derive-h100.txt section c). uniform_first_touch_few_warps_cycles = 60.25 = mean of c.u0.first8.w1 (58 60 61 61 60 61 61 60); uniform_few_warps_limit = 2; uniform_fill_interval_cycles = 0 (held one after the other by C4, no spacing seen); vector_fill_interval_cycles = 27.0 = (4 + 169 - 92.15) / 3 from c.v0.batch4; block_bytes = 256; block_fetch_cycles = 491.1 = mean of (first line of a block) - (first touch): c.u3.first8 loads 1, 4, 8 at the load (695 537 539) - 129.0 and c.v3.first8 loads 1, 4, 8 at the reader (656 574 609) - 92.15.

constant_paths.h100.v2.experimental.description: H100 constant_paths v2 experimental field (tools/microbench/constant_paths/protocol-v2.json; data $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/warp_issue-v2/h100). uniform_first_touch_min_smsps = 2: C5 replaced -- the uniform first touch of a line costs uniform_first_touch_cycles x max(uniform_first_touch_min_smsps, n) / (SMSPs per SM), n = the number of the SM's SMSPs that hold at least one resident warp when the fill starts (wait at the load per first-touch load of c.u0.first8 by warps per SM: 1 warp 60.25, 2 warps 64.6, 3 warps 95.0, 4 warps 127.0, 8 warps 129.0, 16 warps 122.4; per occupied SMSP, counting at least two: 30.1-32.3). Mechanism not identified beyond the dependence (a fill seems to be delivered per SMSP, two at a time at least); the field is experimental.

crossings.constant_cache.h100.r2.description: H100 crossings protocol v2 constant_cache cell (tools/microbench/crossings/protocol-v2.json; probe ldc_chain.cu: register-indexed LDC pointer chase over a 64 KiB __constant__ table, strides 4/64/128/256 B, footprints 256 B-64 KiB, U 64/256, warm = reps >= 1, cold = first traversal after cudaMemcpyToSymbol; per-load latency = OLS slope over U, two runs agree within 0.07 %). Two warm levels: 37.0 cycles up to the 2 KiB L0 knee at every stride, 107.2 beyond it up to the whole 64 KiB bank (no capacity knee inside the bank, capacity_bytes kept at the bank size); same_line = warm S 4 / F 256 B = 37.0; line_bytes = 64 (the smallest stride whose warm latency equals the hit plateau within 5 % of the S4-to-plateau step; S 4 averages 96.1); miss = cold first traversal at S 256 B / F 64 KiB where every one of the 256 loads touches a new line = 406.5 (the other cold cells mix first-touch and re-touch within the chain: S64 F16/32/64 KiB 136.3/206.6/293.0, S128 F32/64 KiB 219.8/316.1). Verdict measured. Replaces same_line 28.02 / hit 93.89 / miss 382.45 / line 256 / capacity 65536 (hopper-prototype ccscan/constcold/paramwarm harness fits, no probe in this repository). Note (engine, 2026-11-05): MemoryHierarchy::constant() keeps a constant line resident for one cycle only (l1_resident_ shared with the data-L1 fallback), so every LDC pays miss until task/constant-cache-residency lands.

descriptor_visibility.h100.r4b.description: H100 descriptor_visibility r4 (protocol.json + 2026-11-05 addenda; GPU-765e9826, driver 570.124.06, sm clock 1980 MHz; probe SASS 8x STG.E.128 + MEMBAR.ALL.GPU publish, UTMACCTL.IV acquire, UTMALDG.2D). dispatch_refill.h100.r1.description: dispatch_refill run 1 (protocol.json addendum 1): the engine's shared refill tick is refuted (measured mean refill gap 330-401 cycles against 5-60 in the replay) and the truncation of serial_ns_per_cta to whole cycles (1.22 -> 1) costs 12-19 % on serial-limited launches; with the per-slot rule and untruncated constants the replay is within 2.6 % on all 28 cells. The refill gap is a per-SM constant in two classes.

dispatch_refill.h100.r4.description: dispatch_refill run 4 (protocol.json addendum 5). Refill gap per SM class over the six spin cells of runs 1, 2, 4 (three cards): fast 150.3 ns (147.0-154.7), slow 183.5 ns (180.5-187.7); the slow class is four whole topology gpcs, {1,2,3,7} on three of the four cards measured and {1,2,3,5} on one -- the mask is the majority set, a declared choice. PREEXIT: a CTA in which it was executed occupies the dispatch serializer for 0.95 x serial_ns_per_cta more (0.586 ns); per CTA, linear in the fraction of CTAs, independent of position and launch attribute; replay within 2.5 % on all 18 cells. The earlier 174.92 ns (hopper-prototype, tail mode) lies between the two classes.

dsmem.h100.unreachable.description: STRUCTURAL unreachable record (dsmem protocol, tools/microbench/dsmem/protocol.json): on sm_90a, ld / st.shared::cluster to a peer CTA (and to the own rank through the cluster window) compile to generic LD.E / ST.E, exactly as on sm_103a, so LDS / STS / STSM never carry a peer rank and the remote_smem = 1 children of storage.shared.{visibility, issue, acceptance_sm} are never selected; the corpus agrees (0 executed LDS / STS / STSM / LD / ST with a peer rank in the 450 single-cluster cases; peer DSMEM traffic is STAS and remote SYNCS arrives, with their own leaves). Values kept as sentinels (visibility 290.03 = hopper-prototype remote dependent-load fit; issue / acceptance 41.24 = hopper-prototype steady cells). Measured for reference, both runs identical: peer ld.shared::cluster dependent-load latency 206.5 cycles (b300 220.5), own rank through the cluster window 51.0 (b300 51.0), plain LDS chain 33.8 (both). Open engine item: own-CTA generic LD / ST in the cluster shared window are marked space shared_cluster and the segment builder maps that code to generic, so the engine times them through the global memory hierarchy.

exec_units.h100.v1.description: exec_units v1 (tools/microbench/exec_units/protocol.json): one warp per SMSP, resident code, 64-instruction body at stall 1 with the yield bit clear. Self cells and VIADD / LOP3 pairs on both devices: VIADD, LEA, MOV and ULOP3 measure 2.02-2.03 cycles per instruction (issue interval 2.0); LOP3, SHF, IADD3, ISETP, PRMT, SEL, FMNMX, UIADD3, USHF, IMAD near 2.0, IMAD.HI near 4.0. The 1.0 single-source interval from alu_forms does not reproduce in this protocol.

form.reexpressed.2026-11-05.description: EXPERIMENTAL form re-expression into the common field_models declaration: constants -> two-knot linear, affine -> linear sampled at the box sizes, multi-axis tables -> the declared axis at the base cell of the other axes (or the base cell as a constant / slope-0 affine). Values at the knots are the predecessor values; no new measurement.

gather_hit.h100.r1.description: gather_hit h100-r1: L2-hit gather loads cost about 32-38 cycles per load instruction regardless of whether the 32 lanes touch 16 or 32 distinct lines; the count that reproduces it (and the load_port_lines cells) is line switches in lane order -- lanes 0-15 on rows 0-15 and lanes 16-31 on the same rows again gives 32 switches like 32 distinct rows. Installs memory.load_port.lane_order = 1 on h100 (port occupancy = switches x one line slot); b300 untested, pinned 0.

global_atomic.h100.r1.same_address_servi.description: MEASURED H100/SM90 same-address atomic service rate, protocol global_atomic r1 (GPU-4a698cd4): red_same plateau over nsm 1/2/4/8/16/32/66/132 = 43.63/43.61 ops/ns (C0/C1/C2 pass; atom_same full-SM within 10% of red_same full-SM) -> two-run mean service time 0.022927 ns. hopper-prototype value 0.022848 (-0.35%).

global_atomic.h100.r2.dependent_round_tr.description: EXPERIMENTAL H100/SM90 dependent global-atomic round trip, protocol addendum 1 r2 cells (GPU-765e9826): atom_chain_addr 1 SM, 64 lines x 6 runs = 384 dependent ATOMG.E.ADD.STRONG.GPU links, pooled line median 402.17 cycles (a-c vs d-f 402.165 vs 402.615, 0.11%; chain histogram 500-bin 44%, 300-bin 33%, 250-bin 17% -- address-bimodal, no address axis) -> 203.27 ns at f_sm 1.979 GHz. hopper-prototype value 150.21 (median over a smaller placement set); r1 saw 213.11 ns on GPU-4a698cd4.

ifetch.h100.r4.experimental.description: Same run, marginal-slope form: stream_l1 = OLS slope of T_warm over lines for L0 < F <= L1 = 19.62 (runs identical), stream_l2 = slope for F > L1 = 49.37 (runs within 0.5 %), stream_cold = free slope above the 64 KiB knot of the engine-form two-segment fit of T_0 = 120.77 (runs within 0.8 %). ifetch.h100.v3.description: ifetch protocol v3 (tools/microbench/ifetch/protocol-v3.json): looped straight-line code of 224-384 lines, warm passes. No miss up to 248 lines; 34 / 76 / 110 / 155 / 197 / 275 missed lines at 256 / 264 / 272 / 280 / 288 / 304 lines (9.3 cycles per line), every line from 320 on: five misses per line over capacity, saturating 64 lines later = a 4-way cache of 64 sets (32 KiB; the loop's own 8-10 lines share it). The earlier 28672 B was the last plateau cell of the coarser v1 sweep. Four warps on the same code give the same numbers.

kernel_boundary.h100.v1.description: H100 kernel_boundary v1 (tools/microbench/kernel_boundary/protocol.json, frozen before the engine change; data $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/warp_issue/h100/reference-{a,b} per launch id and counter group). launch_first_line_cycles = 246.3 (no_instruction per warp on the first pc at the common level, stall group, launch ids 0-3 of both passes, cells a.empty, a.exit_only, a.nop_exit, a.empty.w1, a.empty.w32, a.empty.g4, b.sled.l1; the common level = executions below the median + 100: h100 median 246.3). exit_branch_resolve_cycles = 8 and exit_drain_tail_cycles = 7 (after EXIT with nothing outstanding - a.exit_only, a.nop_exit and the sleds of 8+ lines, counters: branch_resolving 8 on both devices in every cell, drain 7-8 (h100) / 5-6 (b300)).

l1_residency.h100.r2.description: H100 l1_residency protocol v4 (tools/microbench/crossings/l1_residency/protocol-v4.json; probe l1cap.cu v3: one CTA, lane-0 dependent ld.global.ca chase over F = 4..256 KiB in 4 KiB steps, random cyclic 128 B lines, warm then timed pass; --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs, SASS gate ok). The L1 data budget of a launch is set by the shared-memory configuration the driver selects (occupancy rule: smallest supported configuration >= n_res x (dynamic + static + 1 KiB), n_res = min(32 CTAs, 64 warps / block warps, 228 KiB / per-CTA need)), not by the launch's own shared bytes: the 10 default-hint cells (S 0 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 192 KiB x block 32 / 1024) give effective capacity E = 184 / 240 / 20 / 148 / 52 / 116 / 116 / 116 / 52 / 52 KiB with configurations 64 / 8 / 228 / 100 / 196 / 132 / 132 / 132 / 196 / 196 KiB (cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor equals n_res in every cell) and E + configuration = 248 KiB in all 10 cells of both runs (spread 0) -> data_array_bytes = 253952, reserved_bytes = 0 (measured; the 8 KiB below 256 KiB is the unusable part of the array, the same on both devices). The pinned-hint cells (v3 install path, unrealised) show that cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout does not pin the configuration (hint 0 / 4 / 8 / >= 15 % -> 8 / 100 / 164 / 228 KiB at S = 0; 44 % -> 228 at S = 0 but 132 at S = 64 KiB). Replaces the hopper-prototype residency-fit pair 262144 / 8192 (hopper.141c7baf1efeaffc74458450 / hopper.145407ce83c814fd79fd55d8), whose difference 253952 this run reproduces exactly; the engine value is unchanged. Engine finding handed to the engine line: l1_cap_lines should subtract the selected configuration, not the launch's shared bytes.

l2_merge.h100.async_kernel_check.description: cp.async joins the GPC read domain on h100 (domain_gpc = 2), by the kernel check declared in tools/microbench/l2_merge/protocol-v2.json addendum h100_async_kernel_check_2: eight kernels with hardware L2 counters, mean absolute difference of reads per delivered sector 0.183 with the pair domain, 0.114 with the GPC domain (GPC with the 21.75-cycle window 0.158, pair with it 0.236, GPC with the window counted from the shared read service 0.175). The pair domain shares nothing on triton_grouped_gemm_02 / 03 (1.06 / 1.11 against 0.648 / 0.430 on hardware; GPC 0.672 / 0.478). Counterexamples kept: cutlass_dense_cpasync_05 / 06 share 0.24 more than hardware with the GPC domain (0.671 / 0.635 against 0.911 / 0.880), flashinfer_single_prefill_02 0.13 more. This supersedes the earlier five-kernel decision (read_domain_kernel_check), which was taken with the converter that gave every commit_group group the 32-copy completion and without the per-GPC read limit.

l2_merge.h100.r1.description: H100 l2_merge protocol (tools/microbench/l2_merge/protocol.json; probe tma_scan.cu = hopper-prototype tma_scan_microbench.cu verbatim except the SM-count bound, set m6r2: one CTA per SM (132 SMs), 24 MB L2-resident footprint, UTMALDG.2D 16 KiB boxes, globaltimer-aligned start, two runs x 5 trials, every config cross-checked with ncu lts__t_bytes.sum; all CTAs on distinct SMs, m0 start spread <= 64 ns). window_cycles = D at the 0.5 crossing of the merged fraction m(D) = 2(1 - lts/SM bytes) of a G = 2 pair whose second member starts D SM cycles later: 240.1 (runs 244.2 / 236.0, agreement 3.4 %) -> measured. max_requests_per_read = argmin_N mean_G |r(G) - ceil(G/N)/G| over the aligned G sweep {2,3,4,6,8,11,12,16,22,32,44,132}: N = 4 in both runs (MAE 0.042 / 0.048 (N = 3: 0.064 / 0.062); r(2..132) = 0.51 0.43 0.37 0.36 0.33 0.32 0.31 0.26 0.29 0.27 0.28 0.27) -> measured. delivered_bytes_per_cycle NOT installed from this run: the SM-side aggregate equals SM count x the per-SM TMA stream rate (30.8 B/cycle/SM, 4065 B/cycle) at every G, i.e. the probe is per-SM latency-bound and does not reach the delivery cap (protocol addendum 2026-11-05). Replaces the hopper-prototype full-GPU scan values window 235 (hopper.cd0cd6500f88dc4a4202a80d, same M6 r2 method, reproduced) and max_requests 3 (hopper.3667abe72c627f7114c32123: N = 3 vs 4 was within 0.02 MAE there too); delivered_bytes_per_cycle keeps hopper.17a05956f82b13ac352f95d5 (M1 r4 LDG lockstep 25.2 TB/s).

l2_merge.h100.r3.delivered.description: H100 l2_merge protocol v2 (tools/microbench/l2_merge/protocol-v2.json; probe ldg_scan.cu = hopper-prototype l2_dram_scan_microbench.cu at 16c47f74 verbatim except the SM-count bound and the CUDA 13 clock attributes; sass gate PASS scan_kernel<false> LDG.E.128 x8; set m1r4: 132 SMs, 24 MB L2-resident footprint split into 132/G slices, G CTAs per slice stream the same 256 MB in lockstep with 1024 threads of ld.global.cg.v4; two runs x 5 trials, every config once under ncu). delivered_bytes_per_cycle = max over the lock configs of the SM-side aggregate per SM cycle = 12807.1 / 12691.1 (run-a / run-b, agree 0.9 %), both at ld_l2g_24mb_g004_lock (25.36 / 25.13 TB/s at 1980 MHz; r = lts/l1tex bytes 0.298, i.e. 70 % of the delivered bytes were merged; dram read 12 MB = L2-resident). Disjoint reference 29.8 B/cycle/SM (3841 aggregate); G 6-132 lock 16.9-23.0 TB/s with 3-13 % trial CV; rot controls 9.4-16.5 TB/s. l2_merge.h100.read_domain.description: L2 reads are shared inside a GPC (placement domain; ids 124..131 with the domain of SM 0), for TMA tile loads and cp.async: lockstep cells by SM id, SMs of different pairs of one block 0.61 (TMA) / 0.53 (cp.async) against 0.515 predicted, SMs of the two blocks of one GPC 0.61 / 0.59 against 0.576, a GPC per slice 0.277 / 0.291 against 0.273 with 4 requests per read; different GPCs 1.00. Protocol tools/microbench/l2_merge/protocol-v2.json addenda read_domain / read_domain_result. Installed for TMA / bulk loads only (domain_gpc = 1): the cp.async kernels with hardware counters share less than this rule simulates (reads per delivered sector 0.86-0.91 on hardware, 0.65-0.81 simulated with the GPC domain, 0.83-1.02 with the pair domain) and the four-warp cp.async cells share less than the one-warp cells (all SMs on one region 0.50 against 0.31), so cp.async keeps the pair domain on h100.

ldgsts_loaded.h100.shared_read_domain.description: L2 read sharing domain = SM ids 2k and 2k+1: one-warp lockstep cp.async cells grouped by SM-id bits, r(mask 1) 0.50-0.52, r(mask 2/4/8) 0.98-1.01, r(mask 3) = r(mask 1); far-apart groups do not share (r 0.88-1.06). Partial sharing across id bits 16 / 32 (r 0.74-0.80) is not modelled. Applied to every merging request kind; for TMA this is an assumption. Derivation and outcome in tools/microbench/ldgsts_loaded/protocol.json addenda shared_read_placement / shared_read_domain.

ldl.h100.memory_hierarchy.description: STRUCTURAL: LDL timing is owned by the memory hierarchy. The converter gives every LDL a local-space memory reference and the engine sends space-local accesses through MemoryHierarchy::load (cpp/core/simulator.cpp memory-access branch: only spaces 1 shared / 3 constant leave that path), so the load-to-use latency comes from the memory.l1 / l2 / dram leaves. The instruction.service issue_interval of LDS (3.752, collapsed predecessor table service_latency.h100.r1.table_collapse) and LDSM (1, predecessor placeholder) occupied the lsu_smsp unit as a second, independent serializer, so back-to-back LDS were spaced by 3.752 and the shared protocol's value never bound; the same interval also delayed every other LSU class on that SMSP. store_flood.h100.r1.description: store_flood protocol v1: 384 lane stores per warp in 48 unrolled groups of 8 with a %clock64 read after each group, W in {1,2,4,8} issuing warps on one SM. Steady-state service per request T = max(floor, sectors + P): P counts the touched 128-B lines containing a partially written 32-B granule, floor 2.0 cycles per request (issue_interval), proportional to W (one service per SM). Installs store_l2.partial_line_cycles = 1.0, store_l2.partial_granule_bytes = 32, store_l2.issue_interval_cycles = 2.0; the measured buffer range 32.6-61.4 covers the installed outstanding_requests 43, which is kept. Experimental until the protocol's engine replay passes.

store_scatter.h100.r1.description: store_scatter protocol v1, committed before GPU data (8267a101). Twenty-four stores with clock reads between stores, distinct address registers; widths 2/4/8/16 B x lane strides width/32/128 B x W=1/2, 16 launches x 64 retained repetitions, two runs. Early issue interval = median gaps 2..4 minus (clock-only gap 2 - 1): 3/3/6/23 cycles, identical across all address geometries, both W and both runs. Contiguous controls reproduce lsu_accept v5. Late queue backpressure depends on geometry and is deliberately not installed as an issue interval. This separates width from sector count, confounded in the original contiguous-only experiment.

structural.issue_group.dispatch_slot.artifact: hopper-prototype cpp/src/engine.cpp (reserve_resource(issue_group, 0, 0.0, warp, now, now + 1)); cyclescope cpp/core/simulator.cpp try_issue (which = 1 loop) and scheduler.policy issue_slots = 1
structural.issue_group.dispatch_slot.description: STRUCTURAL: the predecessor's issue_group_resource (smsp_compute_register_issue) was a per-SMSP dispatch slot reserved for exactly ONE cycle per instance (occupancy now..now+1, interval 0), i.e. the 1 warp-instruction per SMSP per cycle rule that cyclescope already enforces through scheduler.policy.issue_slots = 1. The import bound these 68 classes (FFMA / FADD / FMUL / IADD3 / IMAD / LOP3 / ISETP / FMNMX / MUFU / F2FP / SHFL / S2R / ... plus the U* classes) to uniform_smsp as a second unit, and cyclescope's engine occupies the second unit for the class's own issue_interval (the b300 second-pipe semantics: FFMA2 holds fmaheavy for ~2 cycles), so every ALU / FMA / XU instruction of an SMSP serialised on one unit at 1-8.3 cycles each (MUFU 8.26 blocked a following FADD): a porting defect, not a measured mechanism. Evidence on the single-cluster ledgers (ifp arm, build-main10): fa3_fwd_features_03 RWAIT uniform_smsp 213,894 of 182,572 resource-wait cycles (consumer warps 29 %/warp), flashinfer_sampling_00 370,823, flashmla_dense_decode 32,113 of 37,890; with the binding removed the same cases drop 4-20 % and the uniform_smsp wait falls to 1-3 k (U* classes only). The binding is now none for these classes, as on b300 (structural.service_owner), the class's own unit (field resource, common/class_resource.json) remains; the U* classes keep resource = uniform_smsp.

structural.pmtrig.no_result.artifact: SASS: PMTRIG is the performance-monitor trigger (cuBLAS / CUTLASS kernels emit it around the main loop); it produces no register result and is consumed by no instruction
structural.pmtrig.no_result.description: STRUCTURAL: PMTRIG retires on the issue frontend in one cycle with no unit, no result latency and no interval — the same ownership rule as the control classes (NOP / YIELD) of service_latency protocol-v2 ownership_rule 'control'.

structural.predicated_off.description: STRUCTURAL: a predicated-off instance retires in one cycle on the issue frontend with no unit, no in-flight cap and no interval, on both devices (the b300 leaf carried max_inflight 1 from the predecessor).

structural.service_owner.description: STRUCTURAL owner rule: the service leaf of a class whose timing is owned by another mechanism (memory.* hierarchy, storage.* TMA / shared / atomic, tensor.pipe) is 1 / 1 / 0 with no cap; predicated-off and unmeasured fields of newly added classes likewise. Also cited by the hopper queue_class field previously sourced from dce10c72aa13.

sync_basic.h100.v2.description: sync_basic installation protocol v5 (tools/microbench/sync_basic/protocol-v5.json) leaves: control.nanosleep.cycles points (request ns, cycles) = the clock cost per sleep of the one-warp cells (derive column 'cost', launch 2): h100 (100, 244.35), (1000, 2024.14), (10000, 31999.47), (100000, 254192.25), (1000000, 1881736.06); and a point at 0 on the line through the first two points (46.60) so that requests below 100 ns follow the short law instead of the 100 ns value; the table clamps above 1 ms (the PTX cap). synchronization.mbarrier.release.service_interval_cycles = sum_i(T_i k_i)/sum_i(k_i^2) over the saturated-server cells (s.mbar_self.w4, t.mbar_all.w4, t.mbar_self.w8), k_i = 2 x warps SYNCS instructions per iteration on the SM = 5.67.

tma_store_loaded.h100.gpc_scope.description: Per-GPC limits of the L2 read service and of the store service (tma_store_loaded protocol-v5 addenda gpc_scope / gpc_scope_result / gpc_scope_replay): unshared cp.async reads of the SMs of one GPC reach 1.06 TB/s at 8, 12 and 18 SMs (two runs identical), every SM 7.78 TB/s; reduce TMA stores of one GPC reach 0.53 TB/s at 12 and 18 SMs, plain stores 0.66-0.70 (runs 6 percent apart), so the plain-store value is the reduce limit x 1.25 = 0.663 TB/s (the measured reduce / plain ratio of the GPC limits is 0.75, of the per-SM rates 0.80). Engine replay of the traced cells with these values: per-SM rate 1.01 (stores, one GPC), 0.98 (stores, every SM), 1.03 (reads, one GPC), 0.95 (reads, every SM) of hardware; without them 1.71 and 3.41 on the one-GPC cells.

The test_wait spin control gives 140-225 (median 173.5), not the installed release 87.9 (which came from a same-thread arrive -> try_wait chain that never blocks), so the protocol control fails by construction -> installed as experimental; the cross-warp release itself is to be re-measured by a barrier_release revision.

wgmma_overlap.h100.r7.description: H100 wgmma_overlap r7 (protocol v5; same overlap_v3.cu probe as r6: kernel operand-form streams ffma_ur / ffma_ur_r / fmul_ur / fmul_r / fadd1 / fadd2n / ilp8 / ilp8n / f2fp / mufu8, 176/192 SASS gate; f2fp unrealised - ptxas desugars into LOP3.LUT/FADD helper insts). Verdict C3+C7 experimental (pass_frac 0.895, max_err 0.59); C3+C7+R measured (1.0 pass, max_err 0.465). Facts: uniform-register operands are free (ffma_ur / fmul_ur t ~= 2.0-2.6 same as fadd1); any instruction carrying a .reuse source flag costs 3.75-4.13 regardless of reads (reuse_flag_floor 4); every op with A in registers (rs) adds alternating +0/+1 on the issuing warpgroup's issues (rs_extra_half_cycles; rs cells: 2.54-2.59 on 2-read, 4.05 on reuse-flagged, ilp8n 3.59); f2fp unrealised; mufu8 9.38 vs base 8.19 (+1.2 unmodelled). Installed: cycles 2, enabled 1, coresident_dependent_half_cycles 1, reuse_flag_floor_cycles 4, rs_extra_half_cycles 1.

wgmma_overlap.h100.v6.description: wgmma_overlap protocol v6 (tools/microbench/wgmma_overlap/protocol-v6.json, addenda 1-6; probe overlap_v4.cu; runs $A/fg-line-cold/wov6/h100-r{1..5}). Launch hold: with one op per commit group the issue of G ops ends at max(21 G, (G - 6) x op time) (n128: 89 / 129 / 169 / 263 / 391 / 1159 cycles for G = 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 12 / 24); with three or six ops per group it is not held (251.5 / 491.5 for G = 12 / 24) -> six pending commit groups. Memory-queue hold: MUFU.EX2, MUFU.RSQ, SHFL.BFLY and shared loads on the SMSPs of the issuing warpgroup's warps -- of another warpgroup's warp and of the owner alike -- do not issue until about seven (6.3-8.8) of its ops are left, whatever the commit grouping (first MUFU / SHFL of the other warp 1144 / 1165 cycles after its window start with six / one op per group, G = 24; FFMA from the first cycle). Not modelled: MUFU 10 against 8.4 cycles after the hold; ops take about 80 instead of 64.5 cycles while another warp runs on the SMSP; two warpgroups issuing at once; Blackwell not measured. The rule first installed from runs 1-3 (launch hold counted ops) was wrong for multi-op groups and is replaced. Installed: only the launch hold (six pending commit groups). The memory-queue hold is measured for one issuing warpgroup but is not installed (both fields 0): run 6 (three warpgroups in a ring, $A/fg-line-cold/wov6/h100-r6) shows that with several issuing warpgroups the engine's op timeline differs from the hardware's (each warpgroup waits about 465 cycles for its first commit group whether or not other warpgroups' ops are in flight; a 15-op section takes 126 cycles alone and 200-1000 in the ring), so the hold would be applied at the wrong times.

queue_basic.h100.v1.description: H100 queue_basic v1 / v2 (one warp, 64-iteration loop, producers in consecutive issue slots, per-pc samples of two reference passes against the replay ledger) and the installation protocol warp_queue v1 (rules Q1-Q5): a per-warp queue of 10 entries with one serial release per warp, release interval per kind and operand width (LDS 2, SHFL.BFLY 2, STS 4 / 8 B 8 / 16 B 10, SHFL.IDX 4, LDG 4, STG 6 / 8 B 8 / 16 B 12 cycles), start = max(free, issue + 5.5 + 0.5 r), a member waits at issue while 10 entries are unreleased (mio_throttle, lg_throttle when the waiter and all entries are global), stores take a turn of r in the return chain 1; the per-SMSP global store interval (storage.global.store_issue) is disabled because ten stores issue one cycle apart.
